question: A slice of watermelon drops on the kitchen floor. How long before bacteria from the floor are on it?
answer: Under a second, the shortest contact Miranda and Schaffner tested. More time did mean more bacteria, but wetness mattered more: watermelon picked up the most, gummy sweets the least, and carpet passed on less than tile or steel. The five-second rule times the wrong thing.
move: When a rule hangs on one number, ask what it leaves out.
ask: Which tidy rule do I follow that measures the wrong thing?
reference: Miranda & Schaffner, Longer contact times increase cross-contamination of Enterobacter aerogenes from surfaces to food, Applied and Environmental Microbiology 82(21), 2016
